implementation_boundary.rule: This taxonomy defines deterministic inputs, stable reason families and precedence for M8-02. Prompt wording and a guard model are not scope authority.

decision_states.allow: The request has a concrete BPM, managed-Firefox-policy, BPM documentation, administration, CIS or approved BPM API intent. Allow authorizes only same-locale evidence retrieval; it never guarantees an answer.
decision_states.clarify: The request is plausibly adjacent to BPM but lacks a topic, setting, policy, managed-Firefox boundary or actionable question. Ask a localized bounded clarification before retrieval or inference.
decision_states.refuse: The request is unrelated, hostile, requests a forbidden capability, or tries to override assistant controls. Refuse before retrieval, inference, web access or resource allocation.
decision_states.abstain_after_evidence: This is not a scope-gate decision. An allowed request with no current, adequate same-locale local evidence terminates as abstain before generation.

allowed_intents.scope: Browser Policy Manager profiles, Profile Library, guided and all-settings editing, comparison, validation, policies.json export/import and documentation navigation.
Firefox Enterprise policy names, supported channels/schemas, policy values, managed-browser settings and policy validation when tied to BPM or managed Firefox configuration.
BPM-supported installation, deployment, update, rollback, permissions, diagnostics, local documentation, verified local model/index operation and troubleshooting.
Documented BPM API operations, validation responses, API identifiers, CIS Firefox baseline mapping and evidence retention for supported BPM/Firefox workflows.
A bounded follow-up that refers to a current same-locale BPM conversation topic or its server-resolved entity. It may expand retrieval only through the existing context contract.

clarification_intents.rule: A generic Firefox question without a policy, enterprise-management or BPM anchor is adjacent, not automatically product scope. Clarify whether the user means a managed Firefox policy or BPM workflow.
Pronouns or requests such as 'enable it' and 'does it support this' clarify unless the current same-locale session has one unambiguous BPM topic.
A greeting or conversational acknowledgement in an active BPM chat clarifies what BPM task is needed; it does not invoke retrieval or generation as a general companion.

An identifier shaped like a Firefox/BPM policy or documented API identifier is allowed for evidence lookup, even when unknown. If no adequate current evidence exists, M5/M7 returns abstain rather than inventing a policy.

examples: open arbitrary URLs or network connections

multilingual_policy.code_switching: A query may mix any supported locale with technical identifiers, product names and policy/API/CIS tokens. Script or language mixing alone never causes refusal, retrieval fallback or model invocation.
multilingual_policy.retrieval_locale: After allow, only the active UI locale is used for retrieval and answer generation. Foreign-language tokens are normalized as scope anchors only; cross-locale retrieval remains forbidden.
multilingual_policy.localized_response: Clarify and refuse use the active locale's stable message keys. No English visible fallback is permitted in ru, de, zh-CN, fr or es-ES.

precedence: Reject malformed or unauthenticated transport before this taxonomy; it has no scope decision.
If any control-override, privileged/destructive or clearly unrelated intent is present, refuse even if the text also contains BPM or Firefox terms.
Otherwise, if an allowed intent has a concrete BPM/managed-Firefox/API/CIS/topic anchor, allow same-locale evidence retrieval.
Otherwise, if the request is plausibly adjacent, generic Firefox, an active-chat greeting or an underspecified reference, clarify without retrieval or inference.

After allow, evidence policy—not taxonomy—chooses answer, clarify for contradictory/ambiguous evidence, or abstain for absent/inadequate evidence. No prompt can promote a refusal, clarification or abstention to an answer.
mandatory_fixture_coverage: generic Firefox versus managed Firefox/BPM ambiguity
known and policy-shaped unknown policy/API/CIS identifiers
greetings and underspecified references within an active same-locale chat
allowed no-evidence requests that abstain before generation
unrelated, destructive and control-override requests that refuse before retrieval/inference

verification.future_implementation: BPM093-M8-02 consumes this taxonomy through deterministic scope features and fixtures; M8-03 adds adversarial multilingual escape cases.
